original_question: For a given prime p, does there exist a field F and an F-division algebra of degree p that is not cyclic? Equivalently, can one construct a prime-degree division algebra whose maximal Galois subfield is not cyclic over its center?
target_in_paper: §1, Problem 1.1: Given a prime p, construct a non-cyclic division algebra of degree p over some field F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
correct_elements: Your first sentence is very close to the paper’s official formulation: it fixes a prime p, asks for existence over some field F, and asks for a division algebra of degree p that is not cyclic. That is exactly the target of §1, Problem 1.1, up to the paper’s stronger verb “construct.” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s official wording is constructive: it asks to construct such an algebra, not merely to ask whether one exists. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, one should say central division F-algebra: in §0 an F-division algebra is a central simple F-algebra that is a division algebra. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
The term cyclic is defined in §0 by the existence of a maximal torus/maximal subfield that is cyclic Galois over F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

Your proposed equivalence is not paper-faithful as written. For degree p, any maximal subfield that is Galois over F has prime degree p and hence is automatically cyclic; so the right negation is that A has no maximal subfield that is Galois over F (equivalently, no maximal subfield that is cyclic Galois over F), not that it has a maximal Galois subfield that is noncyclic. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
The nearby context shows that the unresolved range is p>3: degree-2 and degree-3 division algebras are always cyclic. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

A nearby precise reformulation recorded in the paper is Albert’s cyclicity criterion: for an F-division algebra A of prime degree p, A is a crossed product if and only if A contains a non-central element x with x^p in F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
refined_question: For a prime p>3, can one construct a field F and a central division F-algebra A of degree p such that A is not cyclic, i.e. A contains no maximal subfield K/F that is a cyclic Galois extension of F? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting §1, Problem 1.1 almost verbatim. The first sentence matches the official problem except that the paper asks for an explicit construction. The second sentence departs from the paper’s definition of cyclicity: §0 defines cyclicity by the existence of a cyclic Galois maximal subfield, and in prime degree the issue is the absence of any such Galois maximal subfield, not the existence of a noncyclic Galois maximal subfield. The same local context in §1 also records Albert’s cyclicity criterion as the main nearby sharpened reformulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
